_source: NAC's own photographs of NAC's own installations, supplied by Nick on 15 October 2026. Unlike the generated fixtures in tests/, these are real.
_privacy: Checked on arrival: all seven carry a small EXIF block and NONE carries a GPS IFD, so no customer's location is in them. They are re-encoded again on import, which is what strips the remaining metadata off the copy a customer receives — the result is measured and shown on the Images panel rather than assumed.
_models: THE MODEL NUMBERS ARE NOT RECORDED HERE. The compliance plates are not legible in any of these photographs, and equipmentImagesFor() matches on the model and only on the model — so a guess would put the wrong machine beside somebody's quote, which is the one thing a photograph on a proposal must never do. Each `equipmentModels` is an empty list for Nick to fill from the job, and until he does, none of these is offered as a photograph of any model.
_consent: An installation photograph also needs a suburb and consent before it reaches the gallery. Those are NAC's to record; nothing here assumes them.
_orientation: Every one of these is PORTRAIT. The cover wants one wide landscape shot of a finished install, at least 1600 px across, and none of these is it.

photos.alt: A Fujitsu Airstage outdoor unit installed against a rendered wall beside an electric hot water tank
photos.seen: Fujitsu, Airstage badge. Outdoor condensing unit, single-stack vertical discharge. Isolator mounted on the wall beside it, conduit and drain run dressed down the wall.

photos.alt: A Daikin R32 inverter outdoor unit on mounting feet against a rendered wall
photos.seen: Daikin, INVERTER, R32. Twin-fan outdoor unit on galvanised mounting feet, isolator and conduit to the right.

photos.alt: A Daikin R410A twin-fan outdoor unit mounted beside a window
photos.seen: Daikin, R410A. Twin-fan outdoor unit on feet.

photos.alt: A Daikin VRV IV outdoor unit installed against weatherboard cladding
photos.seen: Daikin, VRV IV, R410A. Single-fan outdoor unit on feet, isolator above on the cladding.

photos.alt: An AirTouch wall console showing four zones and the set temperature
photos.seen: AirTouch console in a glass surround. Four zones — Master, Living, Bed 2 + 3, Office — each at 100%, heating, set to 26 degrees, fan medium.

photos.alt: An AirTouch wall console showing five zones, each with its own set temperature and its own measured room temperature
photos.seen: AirTouch console. Five zones — Living Room, Bedroom 1, 2, 3 and 4 — each with a SET temperature and a MEASURED room temperature beside it (24, 24, 24, 24, 23). A per-zone measured reading means a room temperature sensor in each of those rooms: this is a picture of the sensor upgrade actually working, which is the one thing a price list cannot show.
